findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at class definition
findings.body: AssignmentSource declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, which Python evaluates once when the class is defined rather than for each instance. Every AssignmentSource created after process start will therefore carry the import/startup time instead of its actual creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each assignment source gets a fresh timestamp.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a datetime into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` directly as an apply_async kwarg, and to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict(), so `queued` remains a datetime object. Sentry/Celery task arguments must be serializable (JSON); enqueueing an inbound-triggered assignment can therefore fail to serialize, or in other transports round-trip queued as a string that AssignmentSource.from_dict() never parses back to datetime. Serialize queued with isoformat() in to_dict() and parse it in from_dict() to make the round-trip safe.

findings.title: Task unconditionally passes new assignment_source kwarg to all installations
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` for every issue-sync installation, but the abstract sync_assignee_outbound signature in IssueSyncIntegration was not updated to declare this parameter. Any concrete integration (including out-of-tree or legacy implementations) whose sync_assignee_outbound accepts only external_issue/user/assign (and no **kwargs) will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync, breaking syncs that worked before. Update the abstract contract and all implementations, or only pass the kwarg to implementations that accept it.
